newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-RHODES HELPS NATAL SQUARE FINAL WITH W.P..
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-RHODES HELPS NATAL SQUARE FINAL WITH W.P..

text.p: An unbeaten 46 from man of the match Jonty Rhodes helped Natal square their Standard Bank Cup final with Western Province at one-game all after the second leg at Kingsmead on Sunday.
Chasing 239 to win, Natal secured a three-wicket victory with four balls to spare after number three batsman Doug Watson had paved the way with a confident 60 from just 70 balls.
Western Province won the first leg by six wickets at Newlands on Friday. The two sides now meet in the deciding third leg at Kingsmead on Monday.

Natal, the reigning Supersport Series champions, recovered from the early loss of Lance Klusener in the second over with a well-paced partnership of 88 for the second wicket between Watson and Andrew Hudson (37).
Just when it seemed the home side were on target for a comfortable victory, all-rounder Brian McMillan came into the W.P. attack and stole back the initiative with two wickets in his first two overs.

Watson, who had struck his seventh 50 in the new competition, was a little unfortunate to be adjudged leg before wicket to McMillan with the ball striking him a little high and possibly destined to miss leg-stump.
From 123 for two, Natal declined to 126 for four before Jonty Rhodes, Derek Crookes (25) and captain Dale Benkenstein (22) batted their side to victory.
Despite accurate bowling from Alan Dawson, with 2-37, and McMillan, with 2-24, Natal were always able to keep up with the required rate.
Rhodes collected his 46 off just 48 balls but Shaun Pollock (12 not out) hit the winning runs when he clipped Craig Matthews through mid wicket for two.
Earlier, a quickfire 27 not out from all-rounder Alan Dawson elevated Western Province to a impressive 238 for seven after they won the toss.

Dawson struck his runs from just 11 balls with two sixes and two fours as the visitors took advantage of a pitch offering a little pace and bounce and some erratic bowling from Lance Klusener and Dale Benkenstein.

Western Province began solidly with a first-wicket stand of 86 in 20 overs between Gary Kirsten (63) and Herschelle Gibbs (40) and H.D. Ackerman (42) and McMillan (31) later upped the tempo with a fourth-wicket partnership of 63 at a run a ball.
Off-spinner Pat Symcox was the pick of the Natal attack with a tidy return of 9-0-30-1.
